title: Hidden Dyson Universality in Inverse-Spectral Geometry
abstract: Dyson universality typically manifests itself in local eigenvalue statistics. Here we show that its signature survives a nonlinear inverse-spectral reconstruction and reappears in the matrix geometry of the reconstructed operator. Using a dressing transformation, we map each unfolded spectrum to a deformation $f(x)$ of a fixed harmonic oscillator and represent it in the common oscillator basis by $F_{mn}=\bra m|f|n\ket$. We resolve the matrix-element weight into shells of fixed distance $d=|m-n|$, corresponding to the energy-transfer channels of the reference oscillator, and characterize the resulting distribution by distance-shell moments. Independently calibrated on Gaussian $β$-ensembles, these moments vary smoothly with $β$ and distinguish the GOE, GUE, and GSE. With this calibration fixed, applying the same diagnostic to the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function places the reconstructed operators in the GUE sector. Thus, the GUE character of the zeros is recovered not through direct statistics of the input levels, but from the distance-resolved geometry of the reconstructed operator.
summary: The paper develops a novel method to test Dyson universality by reconstructing an effective Hamiltonian from known spectra. By analyzing the matrix elements in shells corresponding to energy transfer distances, the authors show that the GUE nature of Riemann zeros is revealed through this geometric structure rather than direct level spacing analysis. This suggests that global spectral geometry can encode deep physical symmetries.
main_problem: The study investigates whether Dyson universality, typically seen in local eigenvalue statistics, can be recovered by analyzing the global geometry of an operator reconstructed from a given spectrum.
main_result: The GUE character of the Riemann zeta function zeros is recovered not from direct level spacing statistics, but from the distance-resolved matrix element geometry of the reconstructed Hamiltonian operator.
method: The authors use an inverse-spectral reconstruction technique involving a dressing transformation to map input spectra (like those from Gaussian ensembles or zeta zeros) onto a deformed harmonic oscillator potential. The resulting operator is then analyzed by resolving its matrix elements into shells based on energy transfer distance.
model_or_system: The analysis compares spectral data from three types of Gaussian $\beta$-ensembles (GOE, GUE, GSE) against the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. A fixed reference harmonic oscillator serves as the basis for reconstructing the effective Hamiltonian $H(s)$.
key_observables: Distance-shell moments ($M^{(s)}_p$) and normalized ratios comparing these moments to the GUE expectation ($R(s/	ext{GUE})_p$).
important_parameters: The Dyson index $\beta$, the moment order $p$ (up to 10), and the height $T$ of the Riemann zeros.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that resolving the matrix element weight into distance shells provides a robust diagnostic tool, and it notes that the residual deviation from GUE decreases with increasing height $T$.
figures_summary: Figures show the continuous variation of moment ratios with $\beta$ (Fig. 1a), compare these ratios for GOE/GUE/GSE vs Riemann zeros (Fig. 1b), and demonstrate that the residual deviation from GUE approaches unity as height $T$ increases (Fig. 2).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the diagnostic using Gaussian $\beta$-ensembles, showing continuous resolution of $\beta$. It then applies this method to Riemann zeros, demonstrating recovery of the GUE sector via distance-resolved geometry. Finally, it performs consistency checks on parameter variations and fractal structure analysis.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-local diagnostic tool for classifying quantum systems based purely on spectral data, suggesting that global geometric properties (like shell moments) can encode fundamental symmetries (Dyson index) even when local statistics are insufficient or obscured.
